MINUTES
  TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE MEETING
  FEBRUARY 20, 2019

1.  CALL TO ORDER

2.  ROLL CALL

  Committee Members Present:  Chair Schmitz, Pope*, Boothe, Combs, Martin,
  Munday, Vanden Bos

  Committee Members Absent:  Scott, Lum

  Staff Members Present:  Greg Grammer, Assistant City Manager
  David Wahba, Planning Director
  Joanne Itagaki, Traffic Engineering Deputy, Willdan
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

  Also Present:  Sgt. Ricky Osburn, LACSD, Lomita Station
  Deputy Tami Bouse, LACSD, Lomita Station

  * Committee Member Pope arrived after Approval of Minutes

  COMMITTEE MEMBER VANDEN BOS, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER COMBS

  APPROVE MINUTES OF THE TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE MEETING

  AYES:  Schmitz, Combs, Vanden Bos

5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

A.  DEEP VALLEY DRIVE PEDESTRIAN CROSSINGS
  Assistant City Manager Grammer stated that at the last Traffic and Safety Committee
  meeting there was a request to review the pedestrian crosswalks on Deep Valley Drive.
  Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki will provide a summary of the report.

  Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki provided a summary of the staff report and included
  exhibits showing the four new developments on Deep Valley Drive which will likely
  increase the number of pedestrians in that area. There are specific guidelines to follow
  with the installation of crosswalks and one of the recommendations is to conduct a study.
  Much of what would need to be studied cannot be done until the projects are completed.

  Consideration should be given to the tools that will be used to attract pedestrians to cross
  at a particular location. Tools that have been used are flashing in-roadway warning lights
  and the rectangular rapid flashing light. Other options are bulb-outs which shortens the
  crossing distance, textured/raised crosswalks, or medians.

  Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that the recommendation is that the Committee
  discuss the pedestrian crossings and provide direction to staff.

Meeting Minutes
Traffic & Safety Committee
February 20, 2019  1
   COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE asked if consideration has been given to put a stop
  sign on Deep Valley Drive at Roxcove for the occupants of the new development at 927
  Deep Valley Drive to safely get to the mall. Planning Director Wahba indicated that this
  improvement might be include in the Peninsula Overlay Zone recommendations. Traffic
  Engineering Deputy Itagaki will research this and inform the Committee as necessary.

  Planning Director Wahba stated that the 927 Deep Valley Drive development should be
  completed in about two years.

  Planning Director Wahba stated that there was a suggestion to put a crosswalk adjacent
  to CVS to lineup with the pedestrian breezeway.

  Deputy Bouse expressed concern with the placement of a crosswalk at this location as it
  could give pedestrians a false sense of security.

  Sergeant Osburn was also concerned about vehicles reaction time when making a turn at
  that location.

  Further discussion ensued on this suggestion.

  CHAIR SCHMITZ asked if it would be prudent to wait until the projects are completed.

  Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki agreed that it would be best to wait until the
  developments begin to open so that studies could be done on the best locations for
  pedestrian crossings.

  The Traffic and Safety Commission agreed to table this item.

  B.  SPEED BOARD LOCATIONS AND ROTATION

  Assistant City Manager Grammer stated that at the last Traffic and Safety Committee
  meeting, questions were asked about the speed board locations and the rotation. Speed
  boards are typically requested by the HOAs when there are speeding issues in their
  neighborhoods. A report on the various requests was provided to the committee. Assistant
  City Manager Grammer noted that the speed board also collects data on the number of
  vehicles and their speed.

  CHAIR SCHMITZ asked if the HOAs are aware that the speed board collects data. This
  information could be useful to the HOA president who could share this with his/her
  members and bring awareness to speeding issues. Assistant City Manager Grammer
  agreed.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER VANDEN BOS expressed his concern with the brightness of the
  speed board at night. Assistant City Manager Grammer stated that he will look into making
  adjustments to the brightness of the speed board.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY inquired about the speed board locations. Assistant
  City Manager Grammer stated that speed boards are placed in locations where the city
  has been notified of a problem with speeding. If an HOA makes a request for a speed
  board in their neighborhood, it will be placed in the rotation until the HOA notifies the city
  that it is no longer needed.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer stated that speed boards are one of many tools that are
  discussed with HOAs who have speeding issues in their neighborhoods.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER POPE asked if anyone has made a request for placement at
  Silver Spur Road between Montemalaga Drive and Palos Verdes Drive North. Traffic
  Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that she met with homeowners on Range Horse Lane
  who had a concern about uphill traffic speeds.

  Jennifer Whynaucht, Hitching Post, requested data for eastbound and westbound traffic
  on Palos Verdes Drive North between Narbonne Avenue/Palos Verdes Drive East and
  Rolling Hills Road stating that there is a lot of speeding in that area.
Meeting Minutes
Traffic & Safety Committee
February 20, 2019  2
 C.  PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH – TRAFFIC SIGNS AND PLACEMENT OF
  FLASHING YELLOW BEACON

  Assistant City Manager Grammer stated that this is a continuation from the last meeting
  where discussion was held regarding speeding on Palos Verdes Drive North. The
  committee had requested information on the number of signs on Palos Verdes Drive North
  as well as the cost of installing a flashing yellow beacon.
  Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that the signs were reviewed and it was
  determined that there are several signs which could be removed. Staff also identified the
  location of the proposed westbound flashing yellow beacon just before Dapplegray
  Elementary School on the speed limit sign to flash during school start and release time.
  This was discussed at the August 2018 Committee meeting.
  Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that there are two other schools in the area and
  there may be more requests for flashing yellow beacons.
  Assistant City Manager Grammer commented on the “must turn right” sign on Eastvale
  and stated that the city has received numerous complaints at that location.
  After a brief discussion, the committee agreed that removing this sign is appropriate.
  COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
  COMBS to,
  REMOVE THE SIGNS ON PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH AS PRESENTED BY
  STAFF

  AYES:  Schmitz, Combs, Vanden Bos, Pope, Boothe, Martin, Munday
  NOES:
  ABSENT:  Scott, Lum
  ABSTAIN:

  Jennifer Whynaucht stated that she represents the walking parents and children of
  Dapplegray School and expressed her concern with the walking path and the speed that
  vehicles travel in that area. Ms. Whynaucht stated that the flashing yellow beacon may be
  more effective closer to Strawberry Lane.

  In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER VANDEN BOS, Traffic Engineering
  Deputy Itagaki stated that it may be better to move the 25 mph further from the school and
  stated that there are guidelines for how far the signs need to be from the school. Traffic
  Engineering Deputy Itagaki would move the sign, if possible, to accommodate this request.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER VANDEN BOS made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE
  MEMBER MUNDAY to,

  MAKE A RECOMMENDATION TO THE CITY COUNCIL TO INSTALL A YELLOW
  FLASHING BEACON FOR WESTBOUND TRAFFIC ON PALOS VERDES DRIVE
  NORTH EAST OF DAPPLEGRAY SCHOOL DURING SCHOOL START AND
  RELEASE TIMES

  AYES:  Schmitz, Combs, Vanden Bos, Pope, Boothe, Martin, Munday
  NOES:
  ABSENT:  Scott, Lum
  ABSTAIN:
